weeks.baby: The tiny embryo has settled into the lining of your womb and the placenta is starting to form.
weeks.you: A missed period is often the first sign. Feeling tired or a little bloated is common.

checklist.text: Book your first visit with a gynaecologist
Ask your doctor about folic acid if you are not already taking it

weeks.baby: The neural tube, which becomes the brain and spine, is forming, and a simple heart has begun to beat.
weeks.you: Nausea, tender breasts and needing to pass urine more often may begin now.

checklist.text: Write down every medicine and supplement you take, to show your doctor

weeks.baby: Small buds that will become arms and legs appear. An early scan may show the heartbeat flickering.
weeks.you: Morning sickness can happen at any time of day. Small, frequent meals often sit better.

checklist.text: Keep a light snack, like a few crackers, by your bed

weeks.baby: The brain is growing quickly and the face is beginning to take shape.
weeks.you: Strong smells may bother you, and some favourite foods may suddenly feel wrong.

checklist.text: Your doctor may suggest first blood tests, such as blood group, haemoglobin, sugar and thyroid

weeks.baby: Fingers and toes are forming, and baby is already making small movements you cannot feel yet.
weeks.you: Nausea and tiredness are often strongest around now. Rest when you can.

checklist.text: Ask whether you need a dating scan to confirm your due date

weeks.baby: All the main organs have started to form. From now on, baby is mostly growing and maturing.
weeks.you: Mood swings are common as hormones rise. Be gentle with yourself.

checklist.text: Keep a water bottle within reach through the day

weeks.baby: Tiny nails are forming and the organs have begun to work.
weeks.you: Your waistline may start to thicken, even before a bump shows.

checklist.text: Ask your doctor about the NT scan, usually done between 11 and 14 weeks

weeks.baby: Baby can open and close their hands, and the bones are starting to harden.
weeks.you: For many women, nausea begins to ease over the next few weeks.

checklist.text: Have the NT scan and blood test if your doctor has advised them

weeks.baby: Reflexes are developing. Baby may curl their toes or startle at a touch on your tummy.
weeks.you: The womb is rising out of the pelvis, so you may need the toilet a little less often.

checklist.text: Decide when you would like to share your news, in your own time

weeks.baby: Fingerprints are forming. This is the last week of the first trimester.
weeks.you: Energy often starts to return as you move into the second trimester.

checklist.text: Ask your doctor when to take the Td (tetanus-diphtheria) vaccine

weeks.baby: Baby can make small facial expressions, like squinting and frowning.
weeks.you: Your appetite may come back. Simple, home-cooked meals are a good choice.

checklist.text: If your doctor agrees, start a gentle daily walk

weeks.baby: Baby can sense light through closed eyelids, and the skeleton keeps getting stronger.
weeks.you: Gums may bleed a little when you brush. A soft toothbrush helps.

checklist.text: Book a dental check-up and tell the dentist you are pregnant

weeks.baby: Neck and back muscles are stronger, so baby can hold their head more upright.
weeks.you: Some women feel the first flutters now, often earlier in a second pregnancy.

checklist.text: Ask whether a quadruple marker blood test is advised for you

weeks.baby: A layer of fat is beginning to form under the skin, which will keep baby warm after birth.
weeks.you: Brief twinges low in the belly are common as the ligaments stretch.

checklist.text: Try sleeping on your side with a pillow between your knees

weeks.baby: The ears are in their final position and baby may hear muffled sounds.
weeks.you: Feeling a little dizzy when you stand up quickly is common. Rise slowly.

checklist.text: Book the anomaly scan, usually done between 18 and 22 weeks

weeks.baby: A creamy coating called vernix is forming to protect baby's skin.
weeks.you: Leg cramps, especially at night, may start. Gentle calf stretches can help.

checklist.text: Do a few gentle calf stretches before bed

weeks.baby: Halfway there. Baby swallows fluid and is practising for life outside.
weeks.you: Your bump is probably showing now, and your navel may start to flatten.

checklist.text: Notice when you feel baby move, and when they seem most active

weeks.baby: Baby is swallowing and practising sucking.
weeks.you: Movements may start to feel stronger and more regular.

checklist.text: Spend a few quiet minutes talking or reading to baby

weeks.baby: Eyebrows and eyelids have formed.
weeks.you: Backache is common now. Gentle stretches and good posture can help.

checklist.text: Sit with your back supported and feet flat on the floor

weeks.baby: Baby can hear sounds from outside, a lovely time to read aloud.
weeks.you: Swollen feet are common. Rest with your feet raised when you can.

checklist.text: Rest with your feet up for a few minutes each day

weeks.baby: The lungs are growing branches and tiny air sacs.
weeks.you: The glucose test (GTT) is often done between weeks 24 and 28.

checklist.text: Book the glucose test (GTT) if your doctor has advised it

weeks.baby: Baby responds to your voice and touch.
weeks.you: Heartburn may increase. Smaller meals and not lying down right after eating can help.

checklist.text: Try smaller meals and wait a while before lying down

weeks.baby: The eyes are beginning to open.
weeks.you: As your bump grows, sleeping on your side may feel better.

checklist.text: Set up pillows to support your bump and back at night

weeks.baby: This is the last week of the second trimester.
weeks.you: A good week to plan your third-trimester visits and tests with your doctor.

checklist.text: Ask your doctor how often you should visit in the third trimester

weeks.baby: Baby can blink, and the brain is growing fast.
weeks.you: Visits usually become more frequent from now on.

checklist.text: If your blood group is Rh negative, ask your doctor about the anti-D injection
Get to know baby's usual pattern of movements

weeks.baby: Muscles and lungs keep maturing, and kicks may feel strong.
weeks.you: You may feel short of breath as baby takes up more room.

checklist.text: Slow your pace on stairs and take breaks when you need them

weeks.baby: The fine body hair (lanugo) is starting to disappear.
weeks.you: Tiredness may return. Extra pillows can make sleep more comfortable.

checklist.text: Ask whether a growth scan is planned for you

weeks.baby: All five senses are working, and baby turns their head from side to side.
weeks.you: Practice tightenings (Braxton Hicks) may come and go. Mention them at your next visit.

checklist.text: Note down any questions to ask at your next visit

weeks.baby: Baby is practising breathing movements, and toenails have grown.
weeks.you: Backache and disturbed sleep are common. Rest whenever you can.

checklist.text: Decide on your hospital and ask about visiting the labour ward

weeks.baby: Bones are hardening, though the skull stays soft for birth.
weeks.you: Hands and feet may swell a little. Remove tight rings if they feel snug.

checklist.text: Talk with your doctor about your wishes for the birth

weeks.baby: The lungs and nervous system are maturing well.
weeks.you: You may feel more pressure low in your pelvis.

checklist.text: Plan who will be with you and help at home after the birth

weeks.baby: The kidneys are fully developed. Most growth now is gaining weight.
weeks.you: You may need the toilet more often again as baby moves lower.

checklist.text: Start packing your hospital bag

weeks.baby: Many babies settle head-down around now.
weeks.you: Visits are often weekly from here. Breathing may ease as baby drops.

checklist.text: Keep your pregnancy file and ID together with the hospital bag

weeks.baby: Baby is practising grasping and is getting ready for birth.
weeks.you: Many women feel an urge to tidy and prepare the home.

checklist.text: Get a few baby clothes washed and ready

weeks.baby: The fine body hair has mostly gone, and baby keeps gaining weight.
weeks.you: Rest as much as you can. Short walks may still feel good if your doctor agrees.

checklist.text: Plan a little rest time every day

weeks.baby: Baby is fully ready. The brain keeps growing, even after birth.
weeks.you: Waiting can feel long. Gentle routines help the days pass.

checklist.text: Do something calming you enjoy, like music or a short walk

weeks.baby: Your due date. Only a few babies arrive exactly on it.
weeks.you: Follow your doctor's plan for the coming days.

checklist.text: Confirm the plan with your doctor if baby has not arrived yet

weeks.baby: Baby is still growing and keeping well inside.
weeks.you: Your doctor may check on you and baby more often now.

checklist.text: Go for the extra check-ups your doctor suggests

weeks.baby: Baby is ready to meet you.
weeks.you: Your doctor will guide the next steps for the birth.

checklist.text: Stay in close touch with your doctor
